title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Clock Model and First Counted Day
content:
Two settings shape how a Demurrage and Detention Free Time product measures time on a container: its clock model and its start offset.

## Clock model

- **Separate** — demurrage and detention are timed on two distinct clocks, each measured against its own free days.
- **Combined** — a single merged clock per direction carries both, measured against one merged allowance.

## Start offset

The start offset says how many days separate the event that sets a clock going from the first day that clock actually counts. It is a whole number of days and is shared by every clock of the product.

## Settings by product

| Product | Clock model | Start offset (days) |
|---|---|---|
| AHL Tariff Free Time | separate | 1 |
| AHL Free Time Extension 3 | separate | 1 |
| AHL Free Time Extension 7 | separate | 1 |
| AHL Combined Free Time 14 | combined | 1 |
| AHL Combined Free Time 21 | combined | 1 |
| AHL Contract Free Time 30 | combined | 1 |

## Points of judgement

- The three tariff and extension products are all on the separate model; the two combined products and the contract product are all on the combined model.
- Every product in the range uses an offset of one day, so the first counted day of any clock is the calendar day following its start event. Hypothetical illustration: a start event dated 10 March gives a first counted day of 11 March.
